hook_text: What if the best way to catch more fish was to stop fishing somewhere?
clip_script: In 1964, South Africa drew a line along sixty kilometres of rocky Tsitsikamma coastline and said: no fishing here. It became Africa's oldest marine protected area. Decades later, divers found more fish, and bigger fish, inside the line. Big females lay far more eggs, and their young drift out on the currents to fishing grounds along the coast. That's the spillover effect. Today South Africa has forty-one marine protected areas, alongside parks like Kruger and Addo. The challenge is making sure local fishing families benefit too.
visual_style: A coastline map with a highlighted reserve; underwater footage comparing sparse reefs outside and busy reefs inside; arrows of tiny fish larvae drifting out to fishing boats.
pacing: Question, reveal, explanation, a thoughtful final note.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson on conservation areas and marine reserves.
